chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) met Abdullah ibn Ja'far, so he said: 'O Abdullah! How can the believer be a believer while he is angry at his portion (divine decree) and belittles his status, with Allah being the Ruler over him? And I am the guarantor that whoever does not have in his heart except satisfaction, that if he supplicates to Allah, He will answer him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between contentment with divine decree and the acceptance of supplication in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) defines true faith (*Iman*) as inseparable from inner contentment (*Rida*) with Allah’s decree, warning that dissatisfaction reveals a deficiency in belief. He further establishes a spiritual guarantee that those whose hearts are free from grumbling will have their supplications answered, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology regarding the connection between divine will and human acceptance.
